scene.sit.1: Sit tall at the middle of the keyboard, feet flat.
scene.sit.2: Curve your fingers as if holding a small ball.
scene.findc.1: Black keys come in groups of two and three.
scene.findc.2: C is the white key just left of the group of two black keys.
scene.fingers.1: Your fingers have numbers: the thumb is 1, the little finger is 5.
course.e1.title: Essentials I
course.e1.desc: Rhythm, reading the treble staff and your first left-hand notes.
course.e2.title: Essentials II
course.e2.desc: New notes above G, the F position and shifting your hands.
course.e3.title: Essentials III
course.e3.desc: Sharps, flats, full sheet music and the C major scale.
scene.e1.rests.1: A rest is a beat of silence. Keep counting while you wait.
scene.e1.rests.2: Play, rest, play, rest: one, two, three, four.
scene.e1.lh.1: Your left hand has numbers too: the thumb is 1, the little finger is 5.
scene.e1.lh.2: Little finger on the C below middle C. These notes live on the bass staff.
scene.e1.together.1: Both thumbs near middle C. The left hand holds a long note while the right hand moves.
scene.e1.eighths.1: Two eighth notes fit in one beat. Count: one-and, two-and.

scene.e2.a.1: A is the white key just right of G. Stretch finger 5 up to reach it, then come back.
scene.e2.f.1: Move your thumb to F. Now fingers 1, 2, 3 play F, G, A and finger 5 plays C.
scene.e2.shift.1: Use the rest to move: lift your hand and land the thumb on the new key before the next beat.

scene.e3.waltz.1: In 3/4 time each bar has three beats: ONE, two, three. A dot adds half the note's length.
scene.e3.lhg.1: Move your left hand down: little finger on the G below, thumb on D.
scene.e3.sharp.1: A sharp (♯) raises a note to the very next key on the right. F sharp is the black key just right of F.
scene.e3.flat.1: A flat (♭) lowers a note to the very next key on the left. B flat is the black key just left of B.
scene.e3.scale.1: Play C, D, E with fingers 1, 2, 3, then tuck your thumb under to play F and keep going up to C.
